item.title: CISA warns ransomware gangs are actively exploiting Windows Task Host privilege escalation CVE-2025-60710
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity regulators have updated the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to confirm that active ransomware groups are weaponizing a local privilege escalation flaw in core Windows operating system subroutines. Local attackers possessing unprivileged user credentials leverage the defect to gain full root administrative authority.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-60710 with a CVSS score of 7.8, impacts the Windows Task Host process handling background scheduled tasks across Windows client and server platforms. Extortion groups exploit the flaw during post-exploitation phases to bypass local access controls, elevate permissions to SYSTEM, and unhook protective security agents before deploying automated encryption binaries across internal subnets.
Elevating local process authority to kernel-level SYSTEM privileges destroys host security boundaries. Once an adversary secures root execution via Windows Task Host, they can unhook endpoint detection agents, extract local credential stores, and execute wide-scale ransomware commands across connected enterprise networks.
- Force immediate installation of Microsoft cumulative security updates across all Windows endpoints and Server instances. - Inspect host event logs for anomalous process creations originating from Task Host execution paths under low-privileged accounts. - Enforce strict endpoint protection rules to intercept unverified privilege escalation routines. - Audit local administrative account registries to identify unauthorized user account creations following privilege elevation attempts.
Host operating system safety relies on prompt security patch deployment combined with continuous process monitoring to ensure core system hosts remain completely protected against privilege escalation exploitation. #CodeDefence #Microsoft #Windows #TaskHost #PrivilegeEscalation #Ransomware #CISA #KEV

item.title: GitLab issues emergency out of band patch for critical code injection vulnerability CVE-2026-19478
item.description:
Emergency out-of-band security updates have been distributed for an enterprise DevOps and source code management platform to address a critical code injection defect. The vulnerability permits unauthenticated remote network actors to modify or delete public repository projects and manipulate underlying commit states.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-19478 with a CVSS score of 9.4, impacts GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition. The security issue stems from improper input validation inside GraphQL directive processing handlers. An unauthenticated attacker can format malformed GraphQL requests to bypass authorization controllers, deleting public project repositories and altering project metadata without valid credentials. Security researchers confirmed functional reproduction of the exploit within minutes of initial public disclosure.
Subverting central source code repositories introduces severe software supply chain risks. Armed with project modification access over public code repositories, threat actors can alter application source code, introduce malicious dependencies, and corrupt release artifacts before distribution to production environments.
- Upgrade GitLab installations to emergency patch releases 17.11.1, 17.10.5, or 17.9.8 immediately across self-hosted environments. - Restrict public internet access to GraphQL endpoints on self-hosted GitLab instances, gating access behind zero trust proxies. - Inspect application audit logs for anomalous GraphQL query executions targeting project deletion or state modification handlers. - Verify repository commit histories and project integrity signatures across all public project trees.
DevOps platform protection demands rapid emergency security patching and strict API input validation to ensure central source code repositories remain protected from unauthenticated code injection payloads. #CodeDefence #GitLab #CodeInjection #SupplyChain #AppSec #PatchManagement #DevSecOps

item.title: City Forum campaign uncovers single threat actor scraping Salesforce and ServiceNow portals since 2025
item.description:
Cyber threat research disclosures have exposed a persistent data scraping campaign operating from a single infrastructure node to extract customer records from enterprise cloud portals. The operation relies on compiled automated tooling to systematically query misconfigured public access endpoints.
The threat activity, dubbed the City Forum campaign, originates from a single VPS server address operating under domain infrastructure established in March 2025. Threat actors utilize a custom Go binary transmitting default user-agent strings to query public-facing Salesforce and ServiceNow customer portals across multiple industry verticals. By targeting unauthenticated API endpoints and permissive public access settings, the adversary systematically scrapes customer profile records, internal ticket details, and business contact lists without triggering standard web application firewall filters.
Exposing public access parameters on enterprise SaaS portals presents ongoing corporate data confidentiality risks. When public customer portals permit unmonitored API querying, administrative misconfigurations allow malicious scraping campaigns to harvest sensitive customer databases over extended operational timelines.
- Perform comprehensive permission audits across public Salesforce and ServiceNow customer portals to restrict public read access. - Enforce strict API query rate limiting and IP reputation controls across public web gateway tiers. - Inspect web server ingress logs for high-volume automated traffic originating from IP address 158.220.87.79 or default Go user agents. - Configure Web Application Firewall inspection rules to block unverified automated data extraction queries targeting portal APIs.
Enterprise SaaS platform defense depends on continuous permission auditing and strict API access verification to ensure public web portals do not expose internal customer records to automated scraping operations. #CodeDefence #Salesforce #ServiceNow #DataScraping #CityForum #AppSec #CloudSecurity
